# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

An edge controller manages charging at several electric-vehicle connectors supplied by one electrical branch whose allowable aggregate current is lower than the sum of the connector ratings. Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier. A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors. A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus.

The controller stores, for each active connector, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value. At each allocation interval, the controller subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current. It first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit. The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor.

The branch current sensor is an independent safety input. If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval, the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit. A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero, the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command. The controller then inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator.

The controller can receive remote schedules and authorizations through a network interface, but it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory. During a network outage it continues already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and the independent branch-current safety process. It does not start a newly connected session unless the local token authorizes that connector and has not expired. Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns.

A service input permits an installer to associate connector identifiers with physical contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time and confirming the corresponding connector current sensor. The association is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector. This prevents a wiring-map error from assigning a current limit to the wrong connector.

The disclosed essential relationship is closed-loop allocation using both per-connector current sensing and independent upstream branch sensing, with staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond. Offline authorization, welded-contactor isolation, tamper-evident records, and installation mapping are supported additional features.

1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
4	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
5	
6	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
7	
8	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.
9

1	FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. The description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands, the pilot reports and the connector current sensor reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels.
8	
9	FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.
10	
11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.
12	
13	FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current requested for the session at that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.
14	
15	A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.
16	
17	FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.
18
